newsitem.title: FINLAND: Asset sales boost UPM-Kymmene H1.
newsitem.headline: Asset sales boost UPM-Kymmene H1.

text.p: Europe's largest forestry group UPM-Kymmene on Thursday said asset sales boosted first-half profit with operations actually weaker than the year-ago -- but the market outlook was gradually brightening.
UPM said profit before extraordinary items and tax rose 70 percent to 3.53 billion markka ($643.1 million) against 2.08 billion in the year-ago period.
It booked gains on divestments including a large chunk of shares in compatriot telecoms group Nokia Oy at the operating level.
Net sales were flat at 26.42 billion markka against 26.17 billion, with earnings per share up sharply at 10.20 markka from 6.17.
The result was at the top end of analysts' forecasts in a 3.15-3.57 billion range, but UPM's stock fell on a weak Helsinki bourse, trading down 2.50 markka at 139.50 at 0930 GMT.
"Despite a significant increase in the volume of sales, profitability excluding gains from asset sales was weaker than for the first six months of last year," UPM said in a statement.
It said it expected full-year earnings, excluding gains from asset sales, to be about the same as last year when it posted a 3.56 billion markka profit before extraordinary items.
"Demand for printing and writing papers is expected to grow during the second half of the year, and the capacity utilisation rate will remain high," it said.

It said strong demand and a rise in pulp prices would gradually pave the way for higher paper prices, but prices for magazine paper and newsprint would be lower than during the second half of last year.
UPM also said demand for most of its packaging materials and special products was expected to remain strong. ($ = 5.488 Finnish Markka)
